newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures near highs late, Jan holds $4.60.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures near highs late, Jan holds $4.60.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures traded near highs late Friday to settle higher in a choppy session after holding support early, sources said.

January retested the $4.60 contract high late but was unable to break through the important resistance level. The contract, which expires Tuesday at 1300 EST, settled at $4.573, up 16.4 cents. February finished nine cents higher at $3.920, widening the discount to Jan to 65.3 cents.
"It's all going to be the weather," said one futures trader, noting a return to much below-normal temperatures should push January through the contract high next week.
Conversely, if temperatures are milder-than-expected, January will likely retest the $4.27, then $3.90, he said.
NYMEX said an estimated 43,587 Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 46,323. Open interest for December 19 rose 1,955 to 164,036.

In the cash market, Gulf Coast gas prices were talked about 30 cents lower at about $4.30, while Midcontinent prices declined into the high-$2.20s. New York city-gate gas sold early at $5.15, but prices quickly slipped below the $5 mark to as low as $4.85.
NYMEX January Alberta natgas was untraded but settled 12 cents higher at $1.85.

Physical December prices at the AECO storage hub were higher in the C$2.26-2.31 per gigajoule range, or mid-$1.60s per mmBtu range. The January market was around C$2.27-2.32 per GJ, or low-$1.80s per mmBtu.
NYMEX January Permian natgas settled 21 cents higher at $4.40. NYMEX said an estimated six lots traded.
Physical Permian prices were talked sharply lower around $4.20.
On the KCBT, January settled 13.3 cents higher at $4.463. Deferreds were also steady to higher. Open interest for December 19 rose 243 to 3,051.
